If the answer is yes, be careful.

points.title: Projected annual compounding return as an equity/bond (Book Value model)
points.question: What is the company's projected annual compounding return as an equity/bond? Take the company's average per share return on equity for the last ten years and subtract the average percentage that is not retained and is paid out as a dividend. Use the resulting difference as the rate of growth that the company's book value will grow. sections.heading: Porter's five forces
paragraphs: Competitive Rivalry: Very High (5/5). Operating margin of 4.2% and ROCE of 22.0% set the intensity of competition. Thin margins mean players compete hard on price, so share gains are expensive.
Supplier Power: High (4/5). A gross margin of 22.2% implies suppliers capture the remaining 77.8% of revenue. Concentrated or commodity-linked inputs give suppliers real leverage.

Buyer Power: Moderate (3/5). The gap between gross (22.2%) and operating (4.2%) margin shows how much value is spent winning and serving customers. A fragmented customer base limits any single buyer's negotiating leverage.
Threat Of Substitution: Low (2/5). Cost Advantage + Scale is the primary defence. The product is embedded in customer workflows, which makes substitution costly.
Threat Of New Entry: Low (2/5). Real estate, supplier terms, distribution logistics and membership brand. keep new entrants at bay.
